issues.legal_issue: A later first information report is permissible when it concerns a distinct, broader offence revealed by new factual discoveries rather than the same offence already reported.
material_facts: The first report made general allegations about individual wrongdoing, including irregularities in recruitment, but did not set out the detailed recruitment scam or allege a conspiracy involving numerous officials.

After a detailed preliminary inquiry, the later report described multiple categories of irregularities in the recruitment process, implicated a larger group of officials, and alleged a broader conspiracy.
The High Court’s inquiry concerned the recruitment scam as a whole, not merely the individual conduct described in the first report.
issues.conclusion: The later first information report was maintainable because it concerned a distinct and broader offence, founded on new factual discoveries, rather than the same cause of action as the earlier report.
issues.legal_principle: Although two first information reports cannot ordinarily be maintained for the same offence or cause of action, a later report is permissible where new information reveals a distinct offence or a larger conspiracy with broader ramifications. The inquiry is into whether the matters are the same in substance, not whether some accused or facts overlap. The Court relied on Sections 173(8) and 190 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and on Ram Lal Narang v. State (Delhi Administration), T.T. Antony v. State of Kerala, Kari Choudhary v. Mst. Sita Devi, Upkar Singh v. Ved Prakash, and State of A.P. v. A.S. Peter.

rule.if: criminal_investigation and earlier_report_general_individual_allegations and later_inquiry_reveals_new_facts and later_allegations_describe_broader_conspiracy and later_offence_distinct_in_substance

predicates.criminal_investigation: The matter is a criminal investigation initiated or pursued through reports of alleged offences.
predicates.earlier_report_general_individual_allega: The earlier report described general allegations of individual wrongdoing without setting out the later-discovered broader offence in detail.
predicates.later_inquiry_reveals_new_facts: A later inquiry uncovered factual information not presented in the earlier report.
predicates.later_allegations_describe_broader_consp: The later allegations describe coordinated wrongdoing involving a broader scheme or group of participants.
predicates.later_offence_distinct_in_substance: The offence described in the later report is distinct in substance from the offence described in the earlier report, even if some facts or people overlap.

issues.definition: When a criminal investigation begins with general allegations and a later inquiry uncovers new facts describing a broader conspiracy that is distinct in substance, a later first information report is permissible.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court exercising public interest jurisdiction may direct an independent central agency to investigate a serious, systemic public scandal.
material_facts: A writ proceeding concerning the recruitment selection developed into a public interest inquiry after the High Court formed a prima facie view that systematic fraud had occurred.
A state officer’s inquiry report identified irregularities and recommended investigation by the Vigilance Department.
The State itself proposed that the central agency investigate the recruitment scandal, and later issued the required consent for that agency to investigate.
The High Court sought an independent investigation into a scandal involving numerous officials and allegations against a former minister.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s direction for an investigation by the central agency was within its jurisdiction, particularly because the State had offered to have that agency investigate.
issues.legal_principle: The High Court may exercise its jurisdiction under Article 226 to direct an investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation, including in a public interest proceeding. The Court distinguished inquisitorial public interest litigation from adversarial private interest litigation and relied on the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, including Section 6, the Central Bureau of Investigation Manual, Indian Bank v. Godhara Nagrik Co-operative Credit Society Ltd., and Raju Ramsing Vasave v. Mahesh Deorao Bhavpurkar. It also noted that a fair investigation serves the rights of both accused and victims under Article 21, and that the State has responsibilities to maintain public order and peace.

rule.if: high_court_public_interest_proceeding and serious_systemic_scandal_alleged and independent_investigation_needed and state_offered_central_agency_investigation

predicates.high_court_public_interest_proceeding: The High Court is conducting a public interest proceeding rather than deciding only a private dispute between litigants.
predicates.serious_systemic_scandal_alleged: The material before the High Court alleges a serious scheme of wrongdoing involving multiple officials or a public process.
predicates.independent_investigation_needed: The circumstances support the need for investigation by an agency independent of those implicated in the alleged wrongdoing.
predicates.state_offered_central_agency_investigati: The State proposed that a central investigative agency investigate the matter.

issues.definition: In a public interest proceeding, when a serious systemic scandal is alleged, an independent investigation is needed, and the State has offered a central agency investigation, the High Court may direct that investigation.

issues.legal_issue: The State may transfer an investigation to another agency, including after a police report has been filed in a distinct matter, where the investigation concerns a separate offence or newly disclosed broader conspiracy.
material_facts: A police report had been filed in the earlier investigation before the State and the High Court proceeded to have the recruitment scandal investigated by the central agency.
The State’s decision concerned the recruitment scandal, which was not the offence investigated in the same scope by the earlier report.
The later investigation disclosed a broader conspiracy and offences involving a larger group of officials.
The State exercised its power to consent to the central agency’s investigation.
issues.conclusion: The filing of the earlier police report did not prevent the State from entrusting the distinct recruitment scandal investigation to the central agency.
issues.legal_principle: The State has supervisory authority over investigations and may, having regard to the nature and complexity of an offence, entrust further investigation to another agency, including a central agency. That authority is distinct from a court’s supervision of an investigation under Section 173(8) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The Court relied on Section 3 of the Police Act, 1861, Sections 36 and 173(8) of the Code, and the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act. It distinguished the rule that judicial monitoring ordinarily ends when a charge sheet is filed, discussed in Vineet Narain v. Union of India, State of Bihar v. P.P. Sharma, Union of India v. Sushil Kumar Modi, Rajiv Ranjan Singh v. Union of India, and Sasi Thomas v. State, because the High Court was not monitoring the same investigation or taking over the trial court’s role.

rule.if: criminal_investigation and state_has_supervisory_role and earlier_report_filed_in_different_scope and later_investigation_concerns_distinct_or_newly_discovered_offence

predicates.criminal_investigation: The matter concerns the investigation of alleged criminal offences.
predicates.state_has_supervisory_role: The State is responsible for supervising the investigation and has chosen to entrust investigative work to an agency.
predicates.earlier_report_filed_in_different_scope: A police report has already been filed, but it concerns an investigation that is different in scope from the later investigation.
predicates.later_investigation_concerns_distinct_or: The later investigation concerns a distinct offence or a broader offence newly disclosed by further factual discoveries.

issues.definition: When the State supervises a criminal investigation and an already-reported matter differs in scope from a later investigation into a distinct or newly discovered offence, the State may entrust the investigation to another agency.

issues.legal_issue: The Court may use its power to do complete justice to separate overlapping trial proceedings and protect persons previously cited as witnesses from being examined without their consent.
material_facts: A charge sheet had been filed in the earlier case, and two persons who were later appellants had been cited as witnesses in it.
The central agency’s investigation concerned the recruitment scandal, and material relating to that scandal had been collected for a separate prosecution.
The Court considered that the earlier trial could overlap with the recruitment scandal investigation and issued directions to manage the proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The trial court was directed to segregate the portion of the earlier trial connected with the recruitment scandal; the persons cited as witnesses were not to be examined in that matter without their consent; and relevant investigative material was to be transferred to the court handling the central agency matter.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 142 of the Constitution, the Court may issue directions necessary to do complete justice, including directions to coordinate related trial proceedings and protect persons cited as witnesses from examination without their consent. The Court relied on Divine Retreat Centre v. State of Kerala.

predicates.overlapping_criminal_trials: Two criminal proceedings contain issues or evidence relating to the same alleged course of events.
predicates.prior_case_cites_persons_as_witnesses: The earlier case identifies persons as witnesses rather than accused.
predicates.later_investigation_targets_related_scan: A later investigation concerns a wider scandal related to part of the earlier case.

issues.definition: When criminal proceedings overlap, persons were cited as witnesses in the earlier case, and a later investigation concerns a related wider scandal, the Court may separate the related trial material and require those persons’ consent before examining them.
